questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

options.A: There is overconsumption and overpricing.
options.C: There is underconsumption and under-pricing.
options.D: There is underproduction and overpricing.

questions.questionText: The table shows the results of a cost-benefit analysis of the construction of a new airport. US$ million private cost 400 private benefit 440 social cost 450 social benefit 480 What is the total value, in US$ million, of all the externalities created by construction of the new airport?

A utility-maximising consumer has a fixed income and can choose between good X and good Y. The diagram shows her budget line and different consumption combinations (F, G, H, J, K and L) of products X and Y. F good G Y J H K L O good X Which consumption combinations are currently available to her?

options.A: F, G, H and L
options.C: G, J and L only
options.D: G, H, J and L

What is correct about cartels?

options.A: They are a form of trade union restrictive practice.
options.B: They are a type of industrial merger.
options.C: They are often subject to government investigation.
options.D: They establish a vertical link between firms.

questions.questionText: When output increases in the short run, which statement is correct?

options.A: Average fixed cost first falls and then, beyond some point, rises.
options.B: Average variable cost increases as soon as the law of diminishing marginal returns begins to operate.
options.C: The minimum point of the average total cost curve occurs at a greater level of output than the minimum point of the average variable cost curve.
options.D: When marginal cost reaches its minimum point, average variable cost must be greater than average fixed cost.

questions.questionText: A firm that controlled over 50% of the market successfully merges with its main competitor to form one large company. What is the most likely reason why, from the firm’s point of view, the merger will fail?

options.A: a fall in consumer surplus
options.C: economies of scale
options.D: market dominance

questions.questionText: A government is attempting to achieve allocative efficiency in a nationalised industry. price $ W X Y AC Z MC MR AR O quantity What will the government do?

options.A: It will set price at W and make sub normal profit.
options.B: It will set price at X and the firm will make supernormal profits.
options.C: It will set price at Y and make normal profits.
options.D: It will set price at Z and make a loss.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a sign beside a busy road. This road was recently cleared of 17 bags of litter. Clearing litter puts lives at risk. What is this an example of?

options.A: free good
options.C: merit good
options.D: nudge theory

questions.questionText: Recent research has shown that consumption of some foods might be harmful. A government committee considers how to intervene in the markets. Which intervention is most likely to reduce consumption of these foods without reducing income equality?

options.A: a minimum price for the harmful foods
options.C: an ad valorem tax on the harmful foods
options.D: an indirect tax on the harmful foods

questions.questionText: In which circumstances is a poverty trap least likely to operate?

options.A: A female worker is paid less than a male worker for doing the same job.
options.B: A worker is paid the minimum wage and refuses a higher paid job because net income is lower after tax.
options.C: A worker refuses higher paid work as it means more expensive travel and childcare costs.
options.D: An unemployed worker refuses a job because earnings are less than unemployment benefit.

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to cause the demand for labour in an industry to be inelastic?

options.A: Labour costs are a small percentage of total cost.
options.B: The demand for the final product has a price elasticity of demand that is greater than one.
options.C: The workforce belongs to a strong trade union.
options.D: There is a large pool of readily available labour.

questions.questionText: Which influence is least likely to promote sustainable economic growth in a developing economy?

options.A: high saving rates
options.C: protected property rights
options.D: rapid population growth

questions.questionText: Governments are interested in providing statistics on the standard of living. They measure the value of material goods and services. Non-material characteristics that affect the standard of living cannot easily be measured. What is an example of a non-material characteristic?

options.A: the failure to include unpaid work in the home
options.B: the freedom to make informed economic choices
options.C: the proportion of GNP used for weapons of war
options.D: the removal of taxes from all forms of consumer expenditure

questions.questionText: Two members of the Hernandez family have recently become unemployed. Mariana has lost her job at the local factory, which has closed because of competition from cheaper imports. Alfonso has lost his job as a shop assistant because the sales have dropped during a recession. How would an economist classify these job losses? Mariana Alfonso

options.A: frictional unemployment seasonal unemployment
options.C: structural unemployment cyclical unemployment
options.D: technological unemployment structural unemployment

options.C: decreasing decreasing increasing flexibility taxation interest rate in the labour market

questions.questionText: Which policy combination will reduce the level of national income by the greatest amount?

options.A: decrease direct taxation and increase interest rates
options.B: decrease direct taxation and increase quantitative easing
options.C: increase direct taxation and increase interest rates
options.D: increase direct taxation and increase quantitative easing

questions.questionText: In a closed economy, the marginal propensity to save is 0.1 and the marginal propensity to pay taxes is also 0.1. These values are constant and do not vary with the level of income. What will be the increase in national income if there is an injection of $100 million into the circular flow?

options.A: $1000 million
options.C: $100 million
options.D: $80 million

questions.questionText: What is assumed by Keynesians?

options.A: An increase in supply always creates an equal increase in demand.
options.B: Government intervention is required to manage the economy.
options.C: Prices always adjust so that markets clear.
options.D: The economy always has full employment.

options.A: no no no

options.D: yes yes yes

questions.questionText: Which policy by developed economies would be most beneficial for developing economies?

options.A: a ban on resource exploration by mining companies in developing economies
options.B: restrictions on investment by global firms in developing economies
options.C: the removal of restrictions on emigration of skilled labour from developing economies
options.D: the withdrawal of agricultural subsidies in developed economies

questions.questionText: The natural rate of unemployment in an economy is 5%. What will happen if a government persists in trying to achieve a target rate of unemployment of 3% by expansionary monetary policy?

options.A: an accelerating rate of inflation
options.C: a high but constant rate of inflation
options.D: a negative rate of inflation
